       1             SENATOR FUSCHILLO:  Thank you very much for

       2      being here today, and those that are watching us

       3      live on the Internet throughout the entire country.

       4             My name is Senator Charles Fuschillo, and

       5      I am Chairman of the Senate Transportation

       6      Committee.

       7             And before I start my remarks, I want to

       8      introduce my colleagues.

       9             To my far left is Senator Owen Johnson;

      10             To my esteemed left is

      11      Senator Carl Marcellino;

      12             To my right is Senator Billy Larkin;

      13             And, to his right is Senator Jack Martins.

      14             Today's hearing will focus on how

      15      New York State can use public-private partnerships,

      16      also known as "P3s," to help expedite and fund

      17      transportation improvement projects.

      18             New York's massive transportation

      19      infrastructure, which supports more than

      20      130 billion vehicles-travel miles every year is

      21      facing a serious crisis that requires immediate

      22      action.

      23             Consider that, New York ranks among the

      24      bottom ten states in the nation for both highway and

      25      bridge conditions, according to the New York State





 

                                                                   4
       1      DOT.

       2             Our state should be replacing or

       3      rehabilitating more than 300 bridges, and

       4      1,150 miles of highway-lanes miles each year.

       5             However, in 2009, only 121 bridges and

       6      661 lane-miles were replaced or rehabilitated.

       7             Nearly 6,200 of the state's 17,400 bridges

       8      are either structurally deficient or functionally

       9      obsolete.

      10             The number of correction actions required to

      11      address critical structure-component issues has more

      12      than tripled over the last five years.

      13             We can't solve these problem by relying only

      14      on current funding sources.  Traditional revenue

      15      streams are declining, our project costs continue to

      16      grow.  Both the DOT and MTA lack capital plans which

      17      are funded beyond this year.

      18             Allowing the system to crumble would

      19      devastate our economy and our quality of life.

      20      Forcing already overburdened residents and

      21      businesses to pay even higher taxes and fees and

      22      tolls is certainly not the answer.

      23             We're faced with a challenging problem:  How

      24      do we pay for projects which we can't afford, but

      25      also can't afford to do without?





 

                                                                   5
       1             Challenging problems demand creative

       2      solutions, and that's exactly what P3s can do for

       3      New York State.

       4             P3s have been utilized throughout the

       5      world.

       6             Here in the U.S., 29 other states and

       7      Puerto Rico have enacted laws authorizing

       8      public-private partnerships for highway and bridge

       9      projects.

      10             Given the private sector's vested interest in

      11      completing projects on time and under budget, P3s

      12      have helped expedite projects and contain costs.

      13             They have been used successfully in

      14      New York State before.

      15             The Strategic Asset Management (SAM) report,

      16      which was issued in 2009, noted that JFK Airport

      17      Terminal 4, the JFK Airport AirTrain, and the

      18      rehabilitated Grand Central Terminal were all highly

      19      successful projects funded by P3s.

      20             The same report encouraged New York to

      21      explore P3s as a way to fund other improvement

      22      projects, and specifically identify several ideal

      23      P3s candidates.

      24             P3 would help improve both our infrastructure

      25      and economy.





 

                                                                   6
       1             The U.S. Department of Transportation noted

       2      that 25,000 jobs are created for every $1 billion

       3      spent on transportation infrastructure projects.

       4             For a state with over 744,000 residents who

       5      are unemployed, getting these projects off the

       6      ground is a critical step to helping people get back

       7      to work.

       8             I have introduced legislation, co-sponsored

       9      with my colleagues here today, which would allow

      10      New York State to better utilize this important

      11      tool.

      12             The Innovative Infrastructure Development Act

      13      would give the State DOT, MTA, New York State Bridge

      14      Authority, and New York State Thruway Authority the

      15      flexibility to enter into P3 agreements to finance

      16      and deliver transportation infrastructure projects.

      17             During the course of today's hearing, we will

      18      hear from a number of experts, from government

      19      agencies to private sector, non-profit

      20      organizations, and labor organizations.

      21             These organizations and individuals will

      22      offer their opinions on how New York State can most

      23      effectively use P3s to perform these desperately

      24      needed upgrades.

      25             I want to thank everybody for coming, and my





 

                                                                   7
       1      colleagues here as well.

       2             I also want to thank Farmingdale State for

       3      allowing us to hold the hearing here once again.

       4             Our first speaker --

       5             Do you have anything you want to add?

       6             SENATOR MARCELLINO:  No.

       7             SENATOR FUSCHILLO:  Do you have anything you

       8      want to add?

      10        Senator Martins indicate to the negative.)

      11             SENATOR LARKIN:  Our first speaker is

      12      Stan Gee, Deputy Commissioner of New York State

      13      Department of Transportation.

      14             Stan, thanks so much for being here.

      15             STANLEY GEE:  Good morning.

      16             Good morning, Senators.

      17             Thank you for this opportunity, and thank you

      18      for being here.

      19             My name is Stanley Gee, the executive deputy

      20      commissioner for the New York State Department of

      21      Transportation.

      22             The concept of public-private partnerships as

      23      a tool to accelerate projects through innovative

      24      financing for transportation infrastructure projects

      25      is important.





 

                                                                   8
       1             As you know, Commissioner McDonald provided

       2      testimony before this Committee last May.

       3             And, I appreciate the opportunity to be here

       4      today, and discuss the possibilities that P3s

       5      provide to us, as well as update you of some of our

       6      efforts since this spring.

       7             I'd like to take this opportunity to call out

       8      the professionalism, dedication, and the hard work

       9      of our staff at DOT, especially related to the

      10      recent storm-related recovery and restoration that

      11      we have been under -- has been underway.  New York

      12      DOT's dedicated employees continue to keep our

      13      state's aging transportation system in operation.

      14             Each and every day the Department performs

      15      critical, unscheduled maintenance of our state's

      16      highways and bridges, and immediately responds to

      17      emergencies, to protect the safety of the traveling

      18      public.  In fact, because of our continuing

      19      collective actions, the infrastructure has been

      20      reliable, making it possible for New Yorkers to take

      21      our transportation system for granted.

      22             These recent storm events have been no

      23      exception.  Over the last month, tropical storms

      24      "Irene" and "Lee" damaged about a third of the

      25      state's total highway system, resulting in closure





 

                                                                   9
       1      of nearly 400 road segments and bridges.

       2             As of September 26th, all but 7 bridges and

       3      14 segments have been repaired and reopened.  Those

       4      that remain closed suffered the most extensive

       5      damage and require significant reconstruction or

       6      replacement.

       7             To address the damage caused by

       8      hurricane-related flooding, DOT deployed an average

       9      of 950 workers and 650 pieces of equipment over each

      10      day over the three-week period immediately following

      11      the storms.

      12             New York State DOT fielded teams to complete

      13      approximately 4,600 damage assessments of pavements,

      14      bridges, streams, signals, and utilities.  This

      15      included approximately 2,900 damage estimates on the

      16      state highway system and 1,700 damage assessments on

      17      the local system.

      18             Maintenance crews cleared storm debris,

      19      initiated restoration work on approximately

      20      5,700 miles of roadway, and repaired approximately

      21      1,200 miles of roadway, in response to the two storm

      22      events.

      23             And I would be remiss if I didn't acknowledge

      24      the response of the industry, both the contractors

      25      and labor who responded in force to this





 

                                                                   10
       1      unprecedented situation.

       2             In short, this has been a truly remarkable

       3      response to such an unprecedented number of events,

       4      and I want to applaud the Governor and the

       5      Commissioner for their leadership during this

       6      difficult time.

       7             If nothing else, the recent storm-related

       8      flooding events should bring to the forefront the

       9      critical nature of our transportation

      10      infrastructure, and the transportation -- and

      11      transportation's importance to the state's economy

      12      and quality of life for our citizens.

      13             Too often we take our transportation

      14      infrastructure for granted; that is, at least, until

      15      it's no longer available to us.

      16             More generally, it's clear, the needs of our

      17      infrastructure, like those of the nation, are far

      18      greater than resources available to address such

      19      needs.

      20             Our state's transportation infrastructure,

      21      like most of the northeast, was built before and

      22      during the Eisenhower Interstate Era.

      23             In addition to the infrastructure being old,

      24      it is heavily used, and subject to harsh weather

      25      conditions more so than southern and western states.





 

                                                                   11
       1             These facilities are critical to providing

       2      transportation service that supports the economy and

       3      provides mobility for our citizens and travelers.

       4      But, as these heavily used facilities continue to

       5      age, it is becoming a greater challenge to maintain

       6      them to ensure their continued use.

       7             As one example:  The average age of a bridge

       8      in New York State is 46 years, while the average

       9      life of a bridge is about 50 years.

      10             Consistent with the findings of

      11      two congressionally mandated national transportation

      12      commissioners -- commissions, as well as the

      13      American Association of State Transportation

      14      Officials, New York DOT estimates that meeting

      15      current and projected demands would require nearly

      16      doubling of our current investments in

      17      transportation infrastructure annually from all

      18      levels of government.

      19             Given the fiscal climate, both within the

      20      state and nationally, this is not likely to occur in

      21      the short term.

      22             The use of public-private partnerships

      23      (P3s), including infrastructure banks and other

      24      prog- -- similar programs, should be explored, to

      25      leverage private funding as tools for accelerating





 

                                                                   12
       1      the projects or facilitating delivery of some

       2      projects.

       3             Though innovative financing mechanisms cannot

       4      substitute for the critical need for ongoing,

       5      stable, predictable funding necessary to maintain

       6      the core transportation infrastructure, their use

       7      can serve as a complement to stable and predictable

       8      funding.

       9             New York's current and future transportation

      10      infrastructure needs traditionally have been

      11      addressed through a partnership of federal, state,

      12      and local government resources.

      13             As we discussed in May, the severe fiscal

      14      constraints at all levels of government have had an

      15      impact on the level of current investment, and

      16      presents significant challenges moving forward.

      17             Federal aid has historically comprised about

      18      50 percent of the State's multi-year capital

      19      programs.

      20             At the federal level, the Highway Trust Fund

      21      no longer remains solvent as a user-supported fund,

      22      and has required more than $34 billion in general

      23      fund transfers since federal fiscal year 2008, just

      24      to maintain current funding levels.

      25             In addition, the most recent federal surface





 

                                                                   13
       1      transportation program, known as "SAFETEA-LU,"

       2      expired on September 30, 2009.  The nation's surface

       3      transportation program has been operating under a

       4      series of extensions since then.

       5             Most recently, this past September 16th,

       6      President Obama signed the eighth extension,

       7      authorizing current funding levels through

       8      March 31, 2012.

       9             A critical issue that remains to date,

      10      Congress has not found a way to sufficiently finance

      11      a long-term, multi-year transportation bill.

      12             While Congress and Administration support

      13      increased funding for transportation infrastructure,

      14      neither has identified the resources necessary for

      15      this to occur.

      16             It is fully expected that, absent any clear

      17      ability at the federal level to increase support to

      18      states in maintaining their transportation

      19      infrastructure, Congress will move away from direct

      20      funding and will provide states more flexibility to

      21      leverage the use of limited resources through

      22      innovative financing techniques.

      23             As such, New York should position itself to

      24      leverage innovative financing efforts that Congress

      25      may provide, and such infra- -- and -- such as,





 

                                                                   14
       1      infrastructure banks and public-private

       2      partnerships.

       3             New York State DOT welcomes the opportunity

       4      to utilize innovative finance mechanisms, such as

       5      P3s, infrastructure banks, design-build, and other

       6      similar programs, to leverage the resources

       7      necessary to maintain infrastructure conditions.

       8      This is, however -- some confusion -- there is some

       9      confusion between privatization and

      10      public-private partnerships.

      11             New York State DOT is not advocating for

      12      private companies to own and operate public

      13      facilities; or privatization.  Rather, we support

      14      the use of P3s where it makes sense.

      15             P3s involve the sharing of risk,

      16      responsibilities, and funding, between the

      17      governmental entity and one or more private-sector

      18      partners.

      19             Traditionally, for highway and bridge

      20      projects, New York State DOT has used, what is

      21      referred to as, "design-bid-build" approach.

      22             Under this approach, projects are designed by

      23      the State, put out for bid, and constructed by

      24      private contractors.  The facilities are then

      25      operated and maintained by the State.





 

                                                                   15
       1             While this represents a form of

       2      public-private partnership, most of the

       3      responsibilities and risks associated with project

       4      delivery fall to the State.

       5             New York State DOT believes that P3s would

       6      be helpful tools to have available as we balance the

       7      needs of the transportation system.  This will allow

       8      more leveraging of private-sector expertise, risk,

       9      and finance.

      10             However, these tools would not replace our

      11      traditional means of delivering projects, as only

      12      certain types of projects would be appropriate for

      13      P3s.  Projects that would lend themselves to P3s

      14      need to be able to attract private-sector interest

      15      while providing a benefit to the public.

      16             Approximately 90 percent of New York State

      17      DOT's capital program is devoted to core

      18      infrastructure projects required to maintain the

      19      system in a state of good repair.  Design-bid-build

      20      will continue to be used to deliver the vast

      21      majority of our projects, but we believe there is a

      22      place, and there are opportunities, for P3s.

      23             New York State DOT would be particularly

      24      interested in the ability to use design-build

      25      techniques to accelerate project delivery.





 

                                                                   16
       1             Design-build is a project delivery technique

       2      that allows project design and construction to occur

       3      under a single contract.  It is a tool that has been

       4      widely used, and successfully, over the last decade,

       5      and is available to about 40 state departments of

       6      transportation.

       7             Here in New York, the MTA and the

       8      Port Authority of New York and New Jersey can

       9      utilize design-build.

      10             This technique is also promoted by the

      11      Federal Highway Administration as one of its

      12      15 tools to accelerate project delivery under its

      13      program known as "Every Day Counts."

      14             While New York State DOT does not have the

      15      statutory authority to undertake design-build, under

      16      the authority of Governor Cuomo's Executive

      17      Order 19, issued on September 1st, in response to

      18      the flooding caused by tropical storms "Irene" and

      19      "Lee," the Department has issued a request for

      20      proposals using a modified design-build procurement

      21      process for the emergency repair work along Route 42

      22      in Greene County.

      23             This project consists of replacing

      24      two bridges, reconstructing washed-out roadway

      25      segments, removing debris, undertaking all the





 

                                                                   17
       1      miscellaneous work items needed to restore the

       2      transportation access within this corridor.

       3             This project provides an opportunity to

       4      utilize the design-build delivery method for a

       5      project that includes a series of diverse repairs

       6      within a defined geographic corridor.

       7             The procurement process for this project will

       8      be based on New York State DOT's nationally known

       9      "Design-Build Manual."  Full quality assurance and

      10      quality control will be undertaken throughout the

      11      project.

      12             The Governor's Executive Order has expanded

      13      the array of tools available to respond to the needs

      14      of the State in making required emergency repairs.

      15             To respond to this need for emergency

      16      infrastructure repairs, New York State DOT is using,

      17      not only design-build, but it is also relying on

      18      more traditional mechanisms, including engaging our

      19      State forces, using emergency stand-by contracts,

      20      supplementing existing contracts with orders on

      21      contract, employing a regional job-order contracts,

      22      and undertaking new quick-response contracts.

      23             The design-build delivery technique is one

      24      additional tool available to meet needs where it

      25      makes sense.





 

                                                                   18
       1             Similarly, the ability to undertake P3s,

       2      where appropriate, would expand the Department's

       3      ability to respond to its ongoing infrastructure

       4      needs with the broadest possible array of tools.

       5             Another potential use for P3 techniques would

       6      be to address the State's bridge needs.

       7             Bridges are a prime example of our state's

       8      and the nation's aging infrastructure.

       9             As I mentioned earlier, New York and the

      10      northeast lead the nation in building -- led the

      11      nation in building new freeways more than 50 years

      12      ago, at the dawn of the interstate Eisen- -- of the

      13      Eisenhower Interstate Era, making our

      14      infrastructure, particularly bridges built during

      15      this period, among the first in the nation to age to

      16      a point where replacement will become necessary.

      17             New York State DOT sees an opportunity to use

      18      the design-build technique to address the backlog of

      19      bridge-improvement needs.  DOT's exploring the

      20      possibility of addressing its growing need for

      21      bridge improvements through an

      22      Accelerated Bridge Program.

      23             Currently, 35 percent of the state's

      24      bridges -- nearly 6,200 of the more than

      25      17,400 bridges -- representing about 54 percent of





 

                                                                   19
       1      the deck area of bridges, requires repair.

       2             While safe for travel, they need some form of

       3      work to extend their surface life -- service life.

       4             Of those bridges, about half are local

       5      bridges, 40 percent are state bridges, and the

       6      remaining 10 percent are the responsibility of other

       7      owners, such as the Thruway Authority and the

       8      State Bridge Authority.

       9             I want to make it very clear:  The Department

      10      continues to comply with all federal and state

      11      requirements for bridge inspections, and exceeds

      12      those requirements when the bridge's condition

      13      indicates the need for more frequent inspections.

      14      A bridge in need of repair does not mean the bridge

      15      is unsafe.

      16             The Department's objective under this

      17      program, would be to reduce the number of bridges

      18      requiring repairs or replacement by accelerating

      19      investment.  This would improve bridge conditions

      20      across the state, and decrease the overall cost of

      21      maintaining the bridge system over time.

      22             To further develop this initiative,

      23      New York State DOT held a workshop in May of this

      24      year, that brought together engineering consortia to

      25      discuss all aspects of an Accelerated Bridge





 

                                                                   20
       1      Program, including project selection, delivery, and

       2      finance.

       3             New York State DOT gained valuable insight

       4      from this and further outreach, and has since

       5      considered options for developing such a program.

       6             Enabling legislation for New York State DOT

       7      to utilize this innovative delivery method would be

       8      necessary.

       9             As I conclude, I want to restate:  That

      10      New York State DOT welcomes the opportunity to work

      11      with you on developing and implementing the use of

      12      public-private partnerships, and other similar

      13      innovative finance techniques, to accelerate project

      14      delivery.

      15             While the use of P3s can serve as a

      16      complement to stable and predictable funding, it

      17      needs to be recognized that P3s are not applicable

      18      to most routine and recurring repair and

      19      rehabilitation activities.  As such, the vast

      20      majority of projects delivered by the Department of

      21      Transportation will continue to use the traditional

      22      design-build-bid -- design-bid-build approach.

      23             All options, however, to maximize and

      24      leverage resources should be considered.

      25             New York State DOT appreciates that this





 

                                                                   21
       1      Committee, and its Chairman, is considering

       2      legislation that would expand our ability to take

       3      advantage of a broader array of these techniques.

       4             This will become increasingly important as

       5      Congress, in reauthorizing federal transportation

       6      legislation, will be considering expanding

       7      opportunities to use P3s.

       8             New York State should be in a position to

       9      take full advantage of all funding opportunities.

      10             Thank you again for this opportunity, and for

      11      me to provide this testimony, and to speak to you

      12      today.

      13             Thank you again.
